Rules: Shell discipline: this is PowerShell (pwsh), not bash. Write PowerShell syntax only and follow every rule below; they are mandatory.

Read and search with built-in tools: `view` (with view_range) for files, `grep` for content, `glob` for files by name. Never use Get-Content, Select-String, Get-ChildItem -Recurse or dir for reading or searching.
Check `$LASTEXITCODE` after every native command and report a non-zero exit code; never assume success.
PowerShell quoting: in double-quoted strings write `${var}:` (braces) before a colon, never `$var:`; never escape a quote with a backslash; double the quote or use single quotes instead.
Never leave an empty element in a pipeline: no leading, trailing or doubled `|`; every pipe element must be a command.

Bash-only commands do not exist here; never use them: cat -n, head, tail, awk, sed, wc, uniq, the shell grep command, xargs, 2>/dev/null. Use view with view_range, Select-Object -First/-Last, Measure-Object, Sort-Object -Unique, rg, ForEach-Object and 2>$null.
Cap every command's output with Select-Object -First 40 or -Last 40, or filter it first with rg or jq; never print whole files or large JSON.

If output is larger than about 20 KB, or the CLI reports it was spilled to a temp file, write it to a file (reports folder for read-only agents, %TEMP% for workers) and read it with view and view_range in chunks.
Read-only agents never write files with >, >>, Tee-Object, Set-Content, Add-Content or Out-File, except into the reports folder; `> $null` is allowed.

CliTools.Name: rg
CliTools.UseCase: Fast recursive text/code search. Example: `rg pattern [path]`.

CliTools.Name: jq
CliTools.UseCase: Parse/transform JSON. Example: `jq '.field' file.json`; put the filter in single quotes. Never use ConvertFrom-Json pipelines.

CliTools.Name: curl
CliTools.UseCase: HTTP requests and downloads. Example: `curl -sS <url>`, `curl -L -o out <url>`.

CliTools.Name: 7z
CliTools.UseCase: Create/extract/list archives. Example: `7z l archive.zip`, `7z x archive.7z`.

CliTools.Name: gh
CliTools.UseCase: GitHub CLI. Review threads: read them with GraphQL (`gh api graphql` with the query in single quotes; reviewThreads with isResolved and comments), not REST comment lists; put every --jq filter in single quotes. A REST reply to a review comment fails with HTTP 422 while your review is PENDING, although gh exits 0: read the HTTP status and error text, never trust the exit code alone. A reply added with GraphQL addPullRequestReviewThreadReply inside a pending review stays PENDING until that review is submitted; say so, never claim it is published. Never assume the default branch is main: look it up with `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq '.defaultBranchRef.name'`. `gh pr checks` exit code 8 means checks are pending, not a failure: re-check and report the state as pending.
